        I am an Assistant Professor of Economics in the College of Business
        & Technology at Seattle Pacific University. I specialize in
        Applied Econometrics, Time Series Analysis, Development Economics,
        and Agribusiness.
      

      
        I enjoy helping students connect economic ideas to the choices they
        make every day, from how they spend their time and money to how global
        events shape the prices they see at the store. My goal in the classroom
        is to make economics approachable, engaging, and something students
        can carry with them long after the course ends.
      

      
        In my research, I specialize in Applied Econometrics, Time Series
        Analysis, and Development Economics. My current research focuses on
        how econometric models and time series data can help us understand
        the forces behind food commodity prices.
      

      
        Outside of work, I enjoy being outdoors, driving, traveling, hiking,
        and playing sports. I also love following just about every sport.

This is my first Python analysis post!

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {"Month": ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr"], 
        "Value": [120, 145, 133, 160]}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

ax.bar(df["Month"], df["Value"], color="#2563eb")
ax.set_title("My First Chart")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Quaye, L.-A., and G. Kostandini.


Agribusiness, 0: e70134 · 2026

Development Economics Agribusiness View Paper


Working Papers



Exploring the Dynamics of the El Niño Southern Oscillation and Food Commodity Prices


This study investigates the impact of ENSO on five major commodity prices from 1980 to 2022, using Smooth Transition Autoregressive (STAR) and Smooth Transition Vector Error Correction (STVECM) models to capture nonlinear dynamics and regime shifts triggered by ENSO shocks. Severe temperature deviations are associated with 10–20% price changes, with warmer phases (El Niño) generally lowering prices and cooler phases (La Niña) raising them — findings with significant implications for food security in import-dependent, low-income countries.

Time Series Food Security Under Review



Down the Mississippi: How Barge Rates Affect Corn Basis


Using weekly data from 2014 to 2024, this study applies a Spatial Durbin Model (SDM) with spatial and time fixed effects to examine how barge freight rates influence corn basis along the Mississippi River. Rising freight rates are associated with declining local corn basis, and significant spillover effects show that rate changes in one region affect basis values in neighboring markets.
